messages:
henry: heads up — rolling perf alert on the prod batcher. p99 latency spiked ~120ms for a subset of small-sequence requests starting ~02:50 UTC :eyes:
henry: traced it down to frequent kernel switches between FlashAttention and the fallback kernel when paged-KV page faults interleave with very small batches
maria: can you paste the profile? curious if it's kernel swap overhead or actual compute regressing
henry: short dump from last run:
```
flamegraph: 43% kernel_switch
20% flash_attention_forward
12% paged_kv_page_fault_handler
8% memcopy_async
```
henry: note the kernel_switch node — that's our runtime tearing down/rebinding cuda contexts because the kernel selection flips mid-epic
sasha: that matches my local repro. If batch formation window is too aggressive we end up with 3-4 tiny batches triggering different kernel plans (small-seq vs long-seq kernels) and paged KV inflation nudges it across threshold
kevin: what thresholds are we using currently? batch_token_target=192, kernel_swap_threshold_ratio=0.6, batch_window_ms=6
maria: 192 is good for throughput but for tiny conversations it causes churn. Suggest adding a hysteresis on kernel selection: only allow a swap if new_kernel_score > old_kernel_score + hysteresis_margin AND stable for hysteresis_time_ms
sasha: implemented a quick patch locally: hysteresis_margin=0.08 (8%), hysteresis_time_ms=40. Result: kernel swaps down from ~14/min to ~1/min, p99 drops back ~90ms -> 28ms on repro
henry: also saw paged_kv thrash: when a swap happens we lose KV residency for some heads and then page faults spike, which feeds back to kernel_score since memory pressure raises fallback preference
kevin: ops idea: pin paged KV pages for active sessions while hysteresis window is open. cheaper than swapping kernels frequently. But risk higher GPU memory usage for tail sessions
maria: experiment matrix we ran:
- ctrl: batch_token_target=192, window_ms=6 (baseline)
- e1: hysteresis_margin=0.08, hysteresis_time_ms=40
- e2: batch_token_target=128, window_ms=10, hysteresis_margin=0.05
- e3: pin_kv_on_hysteresis=true, hysteresis_time_ms=50
results (20k requests each):
- ctrl p50/ p95/ p99 = 12ms / 68ms / 124ms
- e1 = 13ms / 34ms / 30ms (p99 improved a lot — most swaps eliminated)
- e2 = 15ms / 48ms / 45ms (better throughput vs ctrl but not as good as e1 for tail)
- e3 = 14ms / 32ms / 31ms (similar to e1 but memory delta +8% GPU usage)
kevin: nice. e1 looks like the sweet spot with minimal memory impact. Are there any edge cases where hysteresis hides a true perf regression (keeps using a bad kernel)?
sasha: yes, risk is sticky bad choice. We mitigated by TTL: after hysteresis_time_ms*10 we re-evaluate aggressively and allow swap if improvement > 3% for 3 consecutive batches
maria: also added metrics: kernel_swap_rate, avg_kv_page_faults_per_batch, kernel_stickiness. dashboards created in console under Runtime/Batcher/KernelHysteresis
infra-bot: deploy triggered for canary cluster "batcher-probe-hyst-canary" at 03:40 UTC (ops:kevin) :rocket:
henry: can we add a quick integration test that injects paged-kv faults (simulated) and verifies p99 under 60ms for 95% of runs? if canary passes we'll roll to stable
kevin: added a loadtest in infra repo: scripts/loadtests/batcher_hyst_fault_inject.sh. Runs 10k sessions with randomized small/long seq and fault_rate=0.02
sasha: notes for follow-up: tune token_budget_target per-model (some decoders are much more sensitive), consider kernel scoring normalization to include page_fault_penalty so selection favors resident KV when eviction cost high
maria: tl;dr — hysteresis + small window bump fixed the oscillation. e1 will be default in canary; e3 if customer opts-in for lower tail at higher memory use
henry: thanks all — will monitor dashboards and mark follow-up if we see any sticky misroutes. :thumbsup:
